findings.evidence: `roadmap/TauCetiRoadmap/RepresentationTheory/CharacterTheory/Suggested.lean:142` specifies `{f | ∃ (V : FDRep k G) (_ : CategoryTheory.Simple V), V.character = f}`, whereas this declaration uses `∃ n ρ, ρ.IsIrreducible ∧ ρ.character = f`.
findings.fix: Add the bridge between `CategoryTheory.Simple (FDRep k G)` and representation irreducibility and state the canonical FDRep-level spanning theorem, retaining the Representation-level result under a distinct helper name if useful.
findings.issue: `irreducibleCharacters_span` quantifies over coordinate-space `Representation`s, while the roadmap’s named public target quantifies over simple `FDRep`s; downstream FDRep character-table work cannot consume this as the specified completeness API.

findings.evidence: The declaration at line 40 rewrites `IsConj x⁻¹ y⁻¹` to the strictly simpler `IsConj x y`, and no competing declaration was found in `mathlib/Mathlib` or `code/TauCeti`.
findings.issue: The new normalization theorem `isConj_inv_iff` is not tagged `@[simp]`, so simplification will not canonically remove simultaneous inverses from conjugacy goals.

findings.evidence: The theorem at line 124 is the sole public characteristic evaluation lemma and rewrites an application to an `if`; the new completeness proof already needs an explicit `rw [classIndicator_apply]` at `Completeness.lean:176`.
findings.issue: `classIndicator_apply`, the defining evaluation rule for the newly public `classIndicator`, lacks `@[simp]`, forcing consumers to invoke it manually instead of obtaining the advertised indicator normal form.

summary: The exposed completeness theorem does not provide the roadmap’s canonical FDRep-level interface, and two new characteristic normalization lemmas lack simp annotations.
